item.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Python in 2026: SALib vs Chaospy vs EasyVVUQ
item.description: Your model has eleven input parameters, four of which are measured with 15 per cent error, and you have been reporting a single deterministic number — a mean from one run at nominal values — as if it were a prediction. That is the most common methodological failure in computational engineering, and it is a statistics problem, not a modelling problem. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) is the discipline of propagating input uncertainty to output uncertainty, and decomposing which inputs actually drive the spread.
